about: Gates-v2 offline evaluation set (docs/design/media-v2-step8-gates-v2.md G2-9). The 10 recorded stories' packages and briefs are HAND-RECONSTRUCTED from the verbatim S8-21/S8-22 texts (scratch league 1634 was deleted); brief rows a story does not mention hold plausible values chosen so the v1 pool contains the coincidences the stories exploited. Negatives are one-clause mutations in which every number is still in the v1 pool. Direction cases (gates-v2 direction fix): the g2-live-1704 cases are VERBATIM live texts, packages and briefs from scratch league 1704 (the recorded stdin payloads); D-cases are one-clause mutations of them.

cases.body:
This is a disaster. Anthony Davis has gone ice cold, and the numbers are ugly.

Over his last 5, Davis is scoring 20.216 points per 36. The rest of the season, he was at 29.180. That is a drop of nearly 9 points per 36. Nobody can wave that away.

It gets worse. His true shooting over the last 5 is 0.517. Before that, he sat at 0.644. That is elite efficiency one week and ordinary efficiency the next.

Think about what that means. He is scoring far less, and he is doing it far less efficiently. That is not a quiet slump. That is a collapse in both volume and quality.

And the timing? Brutal. It is the TRADE_DEADLINE phase, and one of the league's best scorers is producing like a role player. Is this a blip or a warning sign? The facts show 5 games of decline against a season of dominance. I know which sample is bigger. I also know which one is happening right now.

A 29.180 scorer does not become a 20.216 scorer by accident. Something is off, and the box score is screaming about it. Davis needs to fix it fast.
cases.headline: Anthony Davis has fallen off a cliff: 20.216 points per 36 and a 0.517 true shooting mark
cases.label: derived_true
cases.note: 'nearly 9' is 29.180-20.216 rounded; passed v1 because 9 is a brief loss count

cases.body:
This is a disaster. The Toronto Raptors have dropped 15 spots in the standings. 15. Not 2. Not 3. Fifteen.

They now sit at position 20 in the 2026 regular season. That is where contenders go to die.

Let that number sink in. A slide of 15 places does not happen by accident. It happens when a team stops doing everything that wins games. Where is the accountability?

I am not going to soften it. A 15-spot fall is one of the ugliest movements on the board. Toronto is a 17-20 team, and the standings do not care about excuses.

Is this a slump or a real problem? The facts hand us the fall and the current position, and both look terrible. Position 20 is the price of the collapse.

Toronto wants to be taken seriously. Then stop sliding. Every night the Raptors lose ground, the pressure grows. Fans should be furious. I am.
cases.headline: Toronto Raptors have collapsed 15 spots in the standings and nobody should be calm about it
cases.label: rhetorical
cases.note: 'Not 2. Not 3.' are rhetorical, true of nothing; 17-20 is the brief's own-subject row

cases.body:
Victor Wembanyama's recent scoring rise is an efficiency change as well as a volume change. Over his last 5 games he is producing 36.674 points per 36 minutes. His mark for the rest of the season is 28.678, so the window is about 8 points per 36 above his baseline.

True shooting moved with it. He is at 0.713 over the last 5, against 0.639 for the rest of the season. Scoring more while also shooting more efficiently points to the added points coming from better shot quality or more free throws, not simply from more attempts.

The facts attribute the shift to free throws. The free-throw-rate shift is listed at 8.200. A higher free-throw rate raises true shooting directly, because made free throws add points without a field-goal attempt. That fits the two numbers rising together: he is scoring more per minute and getting more of those points from the line.

The data does not say how he is drawing those fouls. It contains no play-type, matchup or lineup information for this stretch, so any claim about scheme or usage would go beyond it. It also does not say whether the rate holds. Five games is a small window, and free-throw rate tends to swing more than shot-making does.

The sample is what it is. The last 5 games show a scorer whose points per 36 and true shooting are both above his own season baseline, with free throws as the listed cause.
cases.headline: Wembanyama's last 5 games: scoring rate up to 36.674 per 36 on a 0.713 true shooting mark
cases.label: derived_true
cases.note: 'about 8 points' is 36.674-28.678=7.996; passes only because 8.200 renders as 8

Phoenix runs a motion offense paired with a drop defense, and the measured numbers push past what the settings declare. The declared pace target is 61, which ranks 7th in the league. The measured pace is 101.265 possessions per game, the most of any team among 30. The team plays faster than its stated target suggests.

The same pattern shows up from the perimeter. The declared three-point bias is 63, and the measured three-point rate is 0.509, also 1st in the league. Motion offense creates its shots through cutting and passing rather than a single ball handler, and here that movement is producing more possessions and more threes than any other roster.

No person chose this scheme, so it is the setup the team was given rather than a coaching decision. Declared and measured figures show no flagged tension, since the ranks run in the same direction as the settings. The gap is one of degree: a 7th-ranked pace target is producing the league's top possession count.

Phoenix sits 10th in the standings at 27-22 as the trade deadline arrives.

The closest game between the Los Angeles Clippers and the Phoenix Suns this season came down to a single point, and it is the kind of margin that keeps a series honest. The Clippers have won 2 of the 3 meetings so far. The Suns have taken 1.

The standings tell a different story than the series does. Phoenix sits 10th, while the Clippers are 16th at 25 wins, on a 3-game streak as the trade deadline arrives. The Suns, in the Clippers' way of things, are the team with the better position and the worse head-to-head record.

Both sides bring familiar names into the next meeting, set for 2027-02-08. Kawhi Leonard and James Harden headline the Clippers. Devin Booker and Mark Williams do the same for Phoenix. The Clippers play an iso-star offense, and the Suns run motion, so the two teams have built their offenses on different ideas about who should take the shot.

The rivalry score stands at 6. With the series tilted toward Los Angeles, the Clippers get another chance to turn a narrow lead into a firmer one.
